validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED, independent of GEM and of gem.wiki's own generic citations (which are mostly boilerplate 'about the company' pages, not pipeline-specific). I went past gem.wiki's harvested refs to Intergas Central Asia (ICA)'s own primary corporate filings and found this exact named asset, 'МГ «Кожасай-КС-12»' (MG Kozhasai-KS12), listed consistently across THREE of ICA's own annual reports as one of the trunk gas pipelines ('МГ') operated by its Aktobe branch (УМГ «Актобе»): 2018 AR (intergas.kz, 80pp, downloaded and read with pdftotext -layout -- the automated url_verifier content-check fails on the Cyrillic string 'Кожасай' for this specific large PDF, a known Cyrillic-extraction false negative, manually confirmed instead), 2019 AR (same host, passes url_verifier on '168'), and 2020 AR (delivered as a .zip; extracted and read the PDF inside directly). It is ALSO in QazaqGaz's own 2024 Integrated Annual Report (IGO 2024, published 2025) current 33-pipeline asset register for ICA (verified live, passes url_verifier on '2017'; Cyrillic substring check fails for the same encoding reason, manually confirmed via pdftotext). So this is a real, currently-operating asset attested by the operator's own filings across at least 2018-2024/25, not a one-off or GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: 'transmission' is correct -- ICA calls it a 'магистральный газопровод' (trunk/main gas pipeline, 'МГ') in the same breath as Bukhara-Ural and Beineu-Bozoy-Shymkent, and QazaqGaz IGO 2024 groups it with the other 9 trunk lines under this UMG. It is a genuine trunk interconnector (see spec notes below on its Bukhara-Ural tie-in), not a gathering/flowline, despite originating at a single field. DUPLICATE: checked against all 39 rows in the Kazakhstan-gas operating roster -- no other row is named Kozhasai or shares its Kozhasai-field origin/KS-12 endpoint; it does not shadow P3944/P3945/P3963 (other Aktobe-region field-to-CS lines), which have distinct field names and distinct lengths. Not in the structural-lead list the orchestrator flagged. Not matched by GulfPub or OSM crosswalks (checked both; neither has an entry corresponding to this pipeline, so no cross-check available there -- this is a small, gathering-adjacent line neither dataset happened to pick up). ATTRIBUTION: Operator 'АО «Интергаз Центральная Азия»' is well-supported -- ICA is the entity self-reporting operation of exactly this named line across four of its own filings (2018/2019/2020 ARs + implicitly via QazaqGaz IGO2024's ICA-scoped register), about as strong as operator self-attestation gets. Owner 'QazaqGaz 100%' is directionally right (ICA has been part of the KazTransGas/QazaqGaz corporate group since well before this pipeline was built, and QazaqGaz's own 2024 IGO explicitly describes ICA as 'являющееся частью Группы компаний АО «КазТрансГаз»'/'part of the KazTransGaz Group of companies'), but I could not independently pin down an explicit 100.00% *share* for this specific asset -- see fills, left UNRESOLVED on the exact percentage rather than fabricate it. One nuance worth flagging for the record, not a correction: ICA's 2019 annual report names the CUSTOMER ('заказчик') for the actual pipe construction as 'АО «КазТрансГазАймак»' -- a separate, distribution-side regional subsidiary of the same group, not ICA itself -- while ICA is the one that has operated the finished line ever since. That is a normal build/operate split within one corporate family, not a misattribution. Location: StartLocation=Kozhasai (the field, in Aktobe region -- confirmed directly, 'Кожасай в Актюбинской области' in the 2019 AR) and EndPrefecture/District=KS12 (a compressor-station code, consistent with how this roster names several other field-to-CS lines, e.g. P3944, P3945, P3947, P3963) are both fine as recorded; StartState/Province, EndLocation and EndState/Province were blank and are filled below.

validity.recommendation: Do not silently accept StartYear1=2017 as settled. It IS independently attested by QazaqGaz's own 2024 corporate-history timeline, but ICA's own, more granular fiscal-year annual reports describe construction work on this exact corridor continuing well past 2017: the 2018 AR (covering FY2018) lists 'completion of construction of CS Kozhasai' as a GOAL for 2019 (not yet done); the 2019 AR (covering FY2019) reports the 168.3km/325mm pipe itself as newly completed THAT year, while completion of the compressor station is pushed to a 2020 goal; and the 2020 AR reports the compressor station ('ДКС «Кожасай»') as 'newly commissioned' during 2020, with the line itself shown as being actively pigged/cleaned on 2020-08-03/04. Flag for Update to reconcile: either 2017 refers only to an initial/lower-capacity tie-in that was substantially rebuilt/expanded 2019-2020 (plausible -- ICA's own 2021-goals list separately calls the 2021 item a CS 'expansion', implying base construction was already done by then), or QazaqGaz's retrospective 2024 timeline over-simplified/mis-dated the milestone. Either way this is a genuine disagreement inside the company's own record, not a case where I can cleanly recommend a replacement year.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's StartYear1=2017 for this row has NO ref today (MISSING_REF), and the citation gem.wiki itself carries for this fact -- 'About the company' (intergas.kz/en/about-the-company/) -- does not actually support it: I fetched that page directly; every occurrence of the string '2017' on it is inside HTML comments about a 2017 presidential address and Expo 2017 Astana, completely unrelated to this pipeline (verified by reading the raw HTML, not just a substring hit). So the wiki's own backing for '2017' is a false attribution -- a real finding in its own right, separate from whether 2017 is the correct year. Independently of gem.wiki, I DID find a source that states 2017 for this exact pipeline: QazaqGaz's 2024 Integrated Annual Report (IGO 2024, qazaqgaz.kz, published 2025), in a corporate-history timeline, carries the entry '2017 - Введен в эксплуатацию магистральный газопровод от месторождения Кожасай до КС-12 МГ «Бухара-Урал»' ('2017 - commissioned the trunk gas pipeline from the Kozhasai field to KS-12 of MG Bukhara-Ural') -- confirmed by extracting the PDF text directly (both -layout and -raw modes) and reading the line immediately preceding/following the '2017' year token in the timeline graphic; url_verifier passes this URL on '2017' live. HOWEVER, ICA's OWN fiscal-year annual reports tell a more drawn-out story that sits awkwardly next to that single retrospective date: the 2018 AR (FY2018) lists, under 'Goals for 2019', 'Завершение строительства КС «Кожасай»' ('completion of construction of CS Kozhasai') -- i.e. as of end-2018 the compressor station was NOT yet finished. The 2019 AR (FY2019), under a section literally titled 'Строительство компрессорной станции Кожасай' ('Construction of CS Kozhasai'), states construction was completed THAT YEAR of the 325mm/168.3km pipeline itself (feeding cleaned gas from the new UKPG-40 gas-treatment unit at the Kozhasai field into MG Bukhara-Ural), while explicitly noting the compressor station needed to actually push that gas into the trunk system still had to be built -- and the SAME report's own 'Goals for 2020' list again carries 'Завершение строительства КС «Кожасай»'. The 2020 AR (FY2020) finally reports, in its energy-efficiency section, that 2020 saw newly-commissioned compressor stations including 'ДКС «Кожасай»' ('вновь введенных в эксплуатацию' = 'newly put into operation'), and separately shows the Kozhasai-KS12 line (325mm, section '0-168km') being actively pigged/cleaned on 2020-08-03/04 -- i.e. flowing gas by mid-2020. The 2020 AR's own 'Tasks for 2021' list then calls the CS Kozhasai item an 'expansion' ('Завершение расширения КС «Кожасай»'), not new construction, implying base commissioning was behind them by 2021. Length (168.00 km) and Diameter (325.00 mm) are BOTH well-supported and NOT in dispute: the 2019 AR states 'газопровода диаметром 325 мм протяженностью 168,3 км' (325mm diameter, 168.3km length) almost exactly matching GEM's 168.00/325.00 (the 0.3km gap is immaterial rounding), and the 2020 AR's pigging-log table independently repeats '325 / 0-168км' for the same line -- two same-origin but textually distinct company documents agreeing precisely. Capacity is genuinely unresolved -- I found no source stating a throughput figure for this specific line (left blank, no fill attempted, per the standing rule against fabricating weak-field numbers).

fills.researcher_notes: QazaqGaz's 2024 (FY2024, published 2025) Integrated Annual Report lists 'МГ «Кожасай – КС-12»' among ICA's current 10-trunk-pipeline/33-compressor-station asset register -- the most recent confirmation of continued operation I could find. Manually confirmed via pdftotext (Cyrillic substring fails the automated checker for this PDF, a known encoding false-negative; the URL itself is live and passes on ASCII tokens like '2017'). Corroborated by ICA's own 2020 AR, which shows the line actively being pigged/cleaned in Aug 2020 -- both same corporate origin, hence tier=medium not high.
Explicitly a 'газопровод' (gas pipeline, 'МГ' = magistral'nyi gazoprovod) carrying cleaned associated gas from the Kozhasai field into the Bukhara-Ural gas trunk system -- unambiguous.

Named and grouped by ICA as one of its 'МГ' trunk pipelines alongside Bukhara-Ural and Beineu-Bozoy-Shymkent, and it interconnects directly with the Bukhara-Ural trunk system -- a genuine transmission interconnector, not a gathering/flow line, despite the single-field origin.

2019 AR states 'протяженностью 168,3 км' (length 168.3 km); ICA's 2020 AR pigging-log table independently repeats '0-168км' for the same line. 168.00 vs 168.3 is immaterial rounding, not a discrepancy. Single corporate origin across two documents -> tier=medium, not high.
2019 AR: 'газопровода диаметром 325 мм' -- exact match. 2020 AR's pigging-log table independently repeats '325' for the same line. Same-origin corroboration only -> tier=medium.
'На месторождении Кожасай в Актюбинской области выполнено строительство ... газопровода' -- explicitly the Kozhasai oil/gas field. Matches.

StartState/Province and EndState/Province were both blank; filling both as Aktobe Region -- the 2019 AR states the Kozhasai field itself is 'в Актюбинской области' (in Aktobe region), and the destination compressor station KS-12 is repeatedly identified in ICA's own reports as 'КС-12 Шалкарского ЛПУ' (KS-12 of the Shalkar Line Production Unit -- Shalkar being a town/district within Aktobe region), which also fills the previously-blank EndLocation as Shalkar. The 2018 AR is the source for the Shalkar/KS-12 pairing; its automated content-check FAILs because it's a large PDF with Cyrillic text the extractor mangles (a documented false-negative class) -- manually confirmed via pdftotext -layout (line ~1751: 'ГПА №1-7 КС-12 Шалкарского ЛПУ'). EndPrefecture/District='KS12' (already on the sheet) is consistent with this and left as-is.

ICA is the entity self-reporting operation of exactly this named line ('МГ «Кожасай-КС-12»') under its Aktobe branch across its own 2018/2019/2020 annual reports and QazaqGaz's 2024 IGO's ICA-scoped register -- consistent over at least 7 years of filings. Same-origin self-attestation, not cross-checked by a third party -> tier=medium despite the consistency.

QazaqGaz's 2024 IGO confirms ICA (this pipeline's operator) 'являющееся частью Группы компаний АО «КазТрансГаз»' (is part of the KazTransGas Group of companies, the group later renamed QazaqGaz), which is directionally consistent with Owner1=QazaqGaz, but I found no source stating an explicit 100.00% ownership share of THIS SPECIFIC ASSET. Note also that the 2019 AR names 'АО «КазТрансГазАймак»' -- a separate distribution-side subsidiary of the same group -- as the construction customer for the pipe itself, which complicates a clean single-owner story without actually contradicting it. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than cite a source for a percentage it doesn't state.

summary: P3946 Kozhasai-KS12 Gas Pipeline: existence/classification/operator/duplicate CONFIRMED via ICA's own 2018/2019/2020 annual reports + QazaqGaz's 2024 IGO (all list this exact named trunk line under ICA's Aktobe branch); Length=168km and Diameter=325mm both corroborated near-exactly by the 2019 AR text and 2020 AR pigging log. CONCERN (spec): StartYear1=2017 is independently attested by QazaqGaz's 2024 corporate-history timeline, but ICA's own fiscal-year annual reports show construction/commissioning of the compressor station needed to actually operate the line running through 2019 (pipe completed) into 2020 (compressor station commissioned) -- flagged as a genuine disagreement inside the company's own record rather than resolved either way; also, gem.wiki's own cited source for 2017 ('about the company' page) does not actually support that date at all (its '2017' hits are unrelated boilerplate). Filled: StartState/Province, EndLocation (Shalkar), EndState/Province (both Aktobe Region). UNRESOLVED: Owner1% (no source states an explicit 100% share); Capacity left blank (no source found).
